author: Dr Ben Miles
description:
Africa’s crust under the Turkana Rift is thinning to just 13 km, marking the first direct observation of “necking” in an active continental rift. This geological process explains both the eventual splitting of Africa and the exceptional preservation of early human fossils in the region.  

Source Article: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-026-71663-x
